scopeNote: Zero model and native turns. No fee/recipe or B9 research, no new Driver, no second ledger, no second database. wave03-b-native cap4 remainder stays UNKNOWN and unspendable; E's pilot grant untouched; nine user instances preserved.

B1.label: actual consumer typing and input refusal

exactOptional.method: requests are built by adding only the keys that carry a value, so absent optional properties are omitted rather than assigned undefined; the property types were not widened and the rule was not relaxed

B1.publicTypes: each of the four modules exports its request, result and refusal shapes plus the transport/hook/gate contracts, so a consumer names what it passes and receives

B2.label: structural executable resolution and redacted diagnostics
B2.shellRemoved: `sh -c command -v <name>` is gone; tokenization lost a valid operator-selected path containing spaces and would also mangle non-ASCII names
B2.structuralLookup: an absolute or slash-containing selection is used verbatim; a bare name is joined against each PATH entry and tested; every candidate is recorded so a failure is diagnosable
B2.symlinkHandling: the executability test follows symlinks, because a symlink to the real binary is a legitimate operator selection
B2.versionFromResolvedFile: the version probe runs the resolved absolute path, so the reported version and the reported digest describe the same file
B2.redaction: the candidate path list is removed from the public projection because it contains PATH entries that can include a home directory; only the count is kept, and full paths stay behind includePrivate
B2.readOnlyScope: no account reset, no global tool upgrade, no network, no model

B3.label: authenticated proof and current resource consumer unchanged
B3.singleProof: VerifiedRunnerInspection through the one WeakMap in recovery-transport.ts; no second registry was created
rules: attempt identity comes from the proof
plain JSON, an empty resource set and an old state never release the barrier

B4.label: B/E refusal protocol agreed on the flat envelope
B4.actualEEnvelope: guardedSend calls send({ protocolVersion, reservationId, ...turn }); the version and reservation id are TOP-level, not nested in an admission descriptor
B4.moduleEntry: review-sender.ts send() takes that flat shape, echoes reservationId back, and refuses with status no_send for want of an owned transport and a measured bound rather than reporting an entry mismatch
stillCovered: clone failure refuses before reserve and transport
a swapped transport method has no effect
concurrent token consumption sends at most once
an unknown outcome does not refund the token
B4.defaultZeroSends: with no bound the default path still sends nothing and refreshes nothing

B5.label: real SQLite and an independent writer process

substrate.database: A's ProductDatabase on a temp file
substrate.writer: real spawned runner-service child process behind a real authenticated socket

B5.b12Corrected: b12 is relabelled as an IN-MEMORY control matrix that does not demonstrate durable recovery; it opens no database, fsyncs nothing and kills no process, so its no-duplicate-begin result was an artefact of not calling begin twice

B6.label: SIGKILL then rebuild from the same SQLite file
boundaries: the duplicate begin is refused by the primary key rather than by convention
the file is reopened through a genuinely new connection after SIGKILL
command rows, attempt identity and epoch high-water all survive
a post-rebuild duplicate begin is still refused
B6.epoch: a lower epoch cannot lower the stored high-water and a higher one raises it

B7.label: epoch persistence proven; unknown-send reconciliation not
B7.proven: epoch high-water is durable and monotonic across a real SIGKILL and a real reopen of the same file
notProven: an old proof releasing a new attempt was covered only in-process by b12, not across a real process boundary
old native RPC ids were not re-pointed at a new session
no cross-process coordinator restart was driven
B7.rfcNeed: a cross-process coordinator epoch store would be needed to close the remaining rows; none was invented and no second database was created

B8.label: main target prepare/activation consumption
B8.note: not started in this pass; no claim is made

B9.label: multi-slot queue, output caps and resumable degradation
B9.note: not started in this pass; no claim is made

limitations: b13 uses a real SQLite file and a real child process but a FIXTURE driver scenario; no installed vendor agent was executed
answer and steer against a real vendor turn, and unknown-send reconciliation, remain untested
the b13 command ledger is a test-owned table over A's real database handle, not a second product schema or a second ledger
stop observed strictly before the start barrier was not reproduced in this pass
B8 and B9 were not reached, so no multi-slot or output-cap claim is made
no current personal-product permission bypass is claimed; the helper findings remain narrowly scoped
